Comments: On March 5, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection in response to the operator's submission of a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug this well.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. Stage of plugging operations was not confirmed during this inspection.E and S plans are present on-site.Access road appears to not have an RCE installed as depicted on the E and S plan. Some gravel/rock is observed, however due to its consistency throughout the entirety of the access road it appears this rock is pre-existing. Surface/vegetation disturbance is also observed beyond the width of the access road near the entrance. No CFS observed to be installed along the access road at this time.Erosion and sedimentation is observed along the access road at three separate points (Photos 6-17). Erosion channels are forming off the access road at all three points with the third one observed to be extending well beyond the access road downslope. No CFS is observed at either of these three areas. The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.Well tag and posting is not observed on site at this time.CFS on-site appears to be installed and functioning properly in accordance with the E and S plan (Photos 21-22).Violations are being issued for accelerated erosion and sedimentation along the access road, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for well tag and posting requirements not met on-site.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up inspection of Seneca's DCNR TR 007 PAD D site in Delmar Township, Tioga County on 3/1/2023 at 1300 hours. The weather was 34 degrees, cloudy, ice/snow mix, winds NNE @3mph. There were a total of eight wells onsite that appeared capable of production. The 134HU, 129HU, 131HU, 229HU, 230HU, 127HU, 128HU and the 133HU were listed in active status in eFacts. Pad material appears to be stockpiled adjacent to the 133HU, 134HU, 229HU, 230HU. An area of the pad appears to currently be a truck staging area. Large puddles were observed on the pad surface with ice over them. Field conductivity of the puddles was measured between 230uS/cm and 830uS/cm. No fluid was observed in the production tank secondary containment. GPUs were all observed within adequate secondary containment. Stray pieces of secondary containment appear to have blown off the side of the well pad and are hung up on compost filter sock stakes.Violations of the following regulations are cited as OUTSTANDING against the DCNR 007 Pad D 229HU, API #117-22085: 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)SWMA 301. An NOV response has not been received from the operator. No additional violations are noted at this time. I departed the site at 1515 hours.

CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/29/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8282742
Permit API: 081-22059
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Jackson Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of an estimated 20 gallons of produced fluid was released to the pad surface on 7/28/26 at 0244. The notification stated that the fluid was sucked up the same day and impacted soil was excavated and containerized. Work crews were rigging down the drilling rig and associated drilling equipment during this inspection. It rained steadily during this inspection and there was a large volume of stormwater on the pad surface. I met with company man John Hulsey upon arriving on the well pad. He told me that the release occurred in the area of the drilling mud tanks when a jet vac leaked and caused produced fluid to be released to the surface of the pad. I inspected the pad surface and secondary containment for the drilling mud tanks. The fluid on the containment had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 288 uS/cm. The fluid on the pad surface immediately adjacent to the containment berms had an EC of 272 uS/cm. Puddles farther away from the containment on the pad surface had similar readings with none greater than 400 uS/cm. Puddles of stormwater on other areas of the well pad had EC readings of less than 300 uS/cm for each puddle measured. No evidence of produced fluid was observed on the pad surface. The well site secondary containment appeared to be in good condition. No holes were observed in the containment liner.Violations noted against well permit 081-22059 and are considered immediately corrected.

Comments: On May 13, 2024 the Department conducted an incident inspection in regards to a spill that occurred at the Sun Mine Well Site (ESCGP-3 issued on 9/11/2023 and expires on 9/10/2028) on May 10, 2024. According to Derek Zofchak of Range Resources, the spill occurred at 12 PM when drill cuttings and soap slurry fluid entered the flare stack eco tank (which normally separates fluids from gas), the float on the pump within the eco tank malfunctioned and as a result, fluid (approximately 30 gallons of drill cuttings and soap slurry) that normally would not get carried over to the flare stack ended up spewing out of the flare stack as a fine mist onto the graveled well pad and well pad fill slope. At the time of the inspection, Range Resources notified the Department that the spill had been remediated. Unconventional: Yes

Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of approximately 15 to 20 gallons of produced fluid. I spoke with Mike Deming, CHK, upon arrival.A faulty or loose hammer fitting allowed the produced fluid to escape piping after flowback was started. The released fluid flowed along the piping creating the impacted area under the piping and around the associated production equipment. Shortly after flowback began, the leak was noticed and flowback was stopped.The impacted area is an irregular shape roughly 31' long by 21' wide and less than 1' deep. Creston was onsite to delineate the impacted area and help guide the remediation. The impacted area is on the northern side of the pad (the cut slope side) where the production equipment is located. Creston will collect confirmation samples to ensure a complete remediation of the affected area.At the time of inspection, there were no further impacts observed outside the delineated area. Due to the location of the release, the full excavation and sampling will be completed after flowback is finished.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). The violations can be closed after cleanup has been completed.

An onsite meeting was scheduled with Petro Erie Inc. and the Department which developed this Inspection Report.Individuals present at the onsite meeting:Harry Rhoades -Owner/Operator of Petro Erie Inc.Chris Rhoades -Driver for Harry RhoadesRob Bechtel -PA DEPRick Willey -PA DEPAlan Wolf -PA DEPLucas Eichner -PA DEPSteve Wells -PA DEPThe meeting was started off by Rob Bechtel stating the reason for the meeting and what was discovered during a previous site inspection on 7/21/2023 with violations cited. It was discussed that there is a potential that the discharge of produced fluid from the tank battery may have impacted the Reno, PA public water supply. The discussion with Mr. Rhoades made him aware of the fact that there are more than several concerns with his lease. The Department recommended that he hire an environmental consultant to help him through the cleanup and reporting process of an Act 2 cleanup regarding the discharge of produced fluid and the potential impact of the Reno public water supply. Other violations were discussed regarding the other wells on his lease. Statements that were made by Mr. Rhoades during the meeting:-He is the only owner/operator of Petro Erie Inc-He pumps the wells on the lease himself-One well on the lease is on a timer and pumps when he is not present-Mr. Rhoades does not know what occurred at the site referring to the discharge of produced fluid-Wants the water of the households in Reno tested-Hauled 3 loads of brine, 1 load hauled by Gavin to disposal in OH and 2 loads hauled by Paul Weaver to a frac job in West Virginia-Stated that the tank battery and the impact area was present when he purchased the lease

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Crank O (03-067) well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 2/7/2024 at 1025 hours. The weather was 35 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the DEP by Repsol. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #378016 is tied to the release in CTS.According to Repsol, on 2/4/2024 at 0840 hours, a spill of approximately 15 gallons of hydraulic fluid was released to the pad surface after a hose on a water truck was found to be leaking. Repsol reported that the release was cleaned up utilizing absorbents and the impacted pad material was recovered and placed in containers for disposal. Repsol reported that no waterways were impacted by the release. During today's inspection, no evidence of any portion of the release remaining could be observed. An environmental consultant was onsite today for proper disposal/removal of the impacted material from the site. Repsol is currently moving equipment offsite and preparing for a workover rig to move in. Silt sock and a gravel berm were installed along the southwestern edge of the pad for sedimentation control (photo #2). Areas surrounding the well pad remain permanently stabilized with vegetated cover or temporarily stabilized with straw. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. No pooled water was observed on the pad surface, outside of secondary containment today.Based on the reported release of ~15 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the pad surface and Repsol's timely remediation of the release, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #015-23837:CSL 402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)SWMA 301The 25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e) violation cited against API #015-23837 on 1/30/2024 remains outstanding at this time.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Columbia and Springfield Townships, Bradford County on 7/21/2025 at 0920 hours. The weather was 65 degrees F with cloudy skies.Remediation efforts are currently underway. A large pit has been excavated around the 7H well (photo #12) and the impacted material is piled onsite for later removal/disposal (photo #14). Repsol plans to have the wellhead reconstructed and then remedial efforts downslope will begin. The extent of downslope impacts off the western corner of the well pad and along the surface waterline in the adjacent field have been delineated. A temporary berm has been installed in the adjacent field, downslope of impacts, to collect fluids as runoff from precipitation occurs (photo #5). The surface waterline has been removed from the impacted area and from the constructed "corner" berm. Numerous areas of distressed vegetation were observed during this inspection (photos #2, 4, 8, 10 and 11).Resource Environmental (Resource), alongside Repsol's construction contractor, began screening and excavating impacted pad material and soils on Friday, 7/18/2025. Repsol reported that all material field measured at >1.0mS/cm is being recovered and stored for later disposal. Material recovered is being placed into lined residual waste containers which are then being covered prior to site departure. Repsol reported that three trucks are running today for removal of the residual waste containers as they are filled. Resource is screening material/soils every few feet, horizontally and vertically, to guide the excavation efforts.Repsol has Larson Design Group working on designing a more permanent type of land design downslope of the pad in order to continue the collection and recovery of fluids. Repsol plans to have a lined sump constructed within the temporary "corner" berm to continue collecting and recovering fluids. A "supervac" water truck is scheduled to arrive tomorrow morning to finish recovering all of the fluids held within the post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) basin. The DEP recommends the following:-continuing fluids and impacted soils recovery-continuing monitoring nearby streams for potential impacts-continuing soil screening/monitoring to determine the extent of the impacts offsiteViolations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301The DEP departed the site at 1100 hours.

Comments: On December 30, 2025, an on-site meeting was held with operator representative Brad Daugherty to discuss outstanding violations and provide clarifications that have been requested in previous inspection reports. This is also a follow-up inspection to IR 4112550. A violation was issued in IR 4088070 for failure to restore the well site by 10/30/2025, in accordance with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A. The Department requested an NOV Response to IR 4088070 from the operator by December 4, 2025.The First Modification to the COA was entered on 5/01/2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites." Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed:Upon arrival, Daugherty presented a copy of the expired ESCGP for this site, which contains the site restoration plans. They are to be stored on site in a weatherproof storage box (photo 1). Daugherty also reported that the contractor who conducted site reclamation possessed a copy of the site restoration on site during the time of IR 4088070. Daugherty proceeded to explain that the operator did not install the super silt fence north of the well site, and reported that its existence was documented before site reclamation (photo 4). Although site stabilization and progress of restoration could not be completely evaluated during this inspection due to the snow cover, it is still evident through the snow cover that the site has not attained greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth (photos 5, 8, and 9). Daugherty stated that reapplication of mulch and seed is tentatively scheduled for January 1, 2026; weather permitting. Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4088070 shall remain outstanding.

Unconventional: No

Municipality: Wetmore Twp

Inspection Date: 3/26/2021
Comments: This spill occurred sometime in the previous few months but was not reported to DEP. It was noted on a routine inspection by WQSS Rob Bechtel and myself en route to check another site. It appears as though a line leaked and allowed an unknown quantity of crude oil to be released to the site. Some volume flowed off the site and entered a spring run/UNT of Twomile Run. Crude oil was apparent in pools in several areas and fresher product was caught in moss lining the channel of the spring. It then appears to have flowed some 300 feet and entered another UNT of Twomile Run. The operator placed a boom in this stream at some point prior to the discovery of this spill by myself. Some sheen was apparent in leaf piles at this point, but no fresh product was noted. The operator was contacted and they were on the lease at the time. Immediate cleanup options were discussed, including installation of two siphon dams in the initial spring run and use of absorbent pads to catch any oil seeping from the banks. Further inspection will be performed as necessary. Violations are noted.

Code §78a.73(b), §78a81(a)(2) and (3), and §78a.85(a)(5) have been cited. Please note that because your company provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, defective cement, for the other annuli where methane was detected. However, Chief is required to comply with the Department¿s regulations, 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, which provides: ¿In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under § 78a.91 ¿ 78a.98 (related to plugging).¿ Therefore, please provide a written response within 30 days of receipt of this Notice of Violation, as to when and how the above listed violations were or will be corrected, and what steps are being taken to prevent their recurrence.
